title: Tax-Aware Retirement Income: FDs, SCSS, and Debt Funds
description: Inflation is eroding the purchasing power of traditional retirement savings like Fixed Deposits, necessitating a diversified approach. Senior Citizens' Saving.

faq.q: What is the primary disadvantage of relying solely on FDs for retirement income?
faq.a: The main disadvantage is that FD interest is fully taxable at your slab rate, and post-tax returns often struggle to keep pace with inflation, eroding your purchasing power over time.

faq.q: How does SCSS offer a better deal than regular FDs for senior citizens?
faq.a: SCSS typically offers a higher interest rate than regular bank FDs and qualifies for Section 80C tax benefits on the invested amount, making it more tax-efficient for eligible individuals.

faq.q: What is the indexation benefit in debt mutual funds?
faq.a: Indexation adjusts the purchase cost of your debt fund units for inflation when calculating long-term capital gains, thereby reducing your taxable gain and the overall tax liability.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money from debt funds regularly like an FD?
faq.a: Yes, you can set up a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) from your debt funds, which allows you to receive a fixed amount at regular intervals, providing a steady income stream.

faq.q: Is the interest from SCSS taxable?
faq.a: Yes, the interest earned from the Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme is fully taxable as per your income tax slab rate.

faq.q: How does inflation impact my retirement income strategy?
faq.a: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of your money. If your retirement income sources don't generate returns that comfortably beat inflation after taxes, your real income will decline over time.
